checkpoint_review: I maintain my disagreement with the Router on the 'Coloration' checkpoint. While the snake appears greyish in shadow, the lit portions of the dorsal surface exhibit the requisite pinkish-brown/reddish-brown hue characteristic of *Carphophis amoenus*. Marking this as failed would be an over-penalization of lighting conditions. I also reaffirm that the 'Eyes' checkpoint is met; the species description explicitly states eyes are 'minute and dark, barely visible,' and the image shows exactly this—tiny dark specks consistent with the biology. All other anatomical checkpoints (head shape, body cylinder, ventral color, scale gloss, uniformity, tail) are visually confirmed.
artifact_review: I stand by my correction regarding the 'second snake.' The object in the lower right is clearly a root or twig (rigid, no head, striated texture), not a biological entity. The Router's severity 3 artifact verdict was a hallucination based on misinterpretation of background clutter. Dismissing this leaves only the minor texture smoothness/plasticity issue (severity ~1.2). This aligns with the perceptual quality auditor's finding of 'slight compression/blur' and the fine-grained classifier's rank-2 prediction (suggesting the model captured the general form but lacked definitive species-specific micro-texture to secure rank-1). No structural defects exist.

Structural integrity is robust (mask confidence 0.95, clean depth map).
